name: TEF Canada
provider: Le français des affaires (CCI Paris Île-de-France)
notes: All four tests must be taken on the same day for the certificate to be recognized.
Results show a score out of 699 and an “équivalence ancien score”; IRCC uses the équivalence ancien score for each ability.

ce.name: Compréhension de l’écrit
ce.format: Multiple choice, 1 point per correct answer, no penalty for wrong answers.
strategy: Answer every question — a blank scores the same as a wrong answer.
Read the question before the document, then scan for the answer.
Correct options usually paraphrase the text instead of copying its words.
About 90 seconds per question: do not get stuck; mark it and move on.

co.name: Compréhension de l’oral
co.format: Multiple choice on recorded documents, 1 point per correct answer.
strategy: Read the question and options before the audio starts.
Listen for the speaker’s intention and attitude, not only facts.
Numbers, dates and times are frequent targets — note them as you hear them.
Each recording is usually played only once: choose and move on.

ee.name: Expression écrite

sections.title: Exprimer et justifier un point de vue
sections.en: Express and justify a point of view

strategy: Section A: keep the article’s journalistic, factual style and tense consistent (passé composé / imparfait); answer who, what, where, when, why.
Section B: state your position clearly, give at least three developed arguments with examples, and use connectors.
Spend 3–5 minutes planning and 3 minutes rereading for agreement and accents.

eo.name: Expression orale
strategy: Section A: you call or meet someone about a document (an ad, a flyer). Ask around 10 varied, polite questions using vous.
Section B: you try to convince a friend to do something presented in a document. Use several arguments, answer objections and stay friendly (tu).
Fill silences with natural connectors and reformulate if you lose a word.
